agog: Very eager or curious to hear/see something
apex: The top or highest part of something
arid: Having little or no rain; too dry for plants
aura: A distinctive atmosphere or quality around someone
avid: Having or showing a keen interest in something
bard: A poet, traditionally one reciting epics
bask: To lie exposed to warmth and light
boon: A thing that is helpful or beneficial
burr: A prickly seed case or a rough edge on metal
cask: A large barrellike container for liquids
chia: A species of flowering plant in the mint family
clew: A ball of thread or a hint (origin of 'clue')
cove: A small sheltered bay on a coastline
crux: The most important or decisive point
czar: An emperor or person with great power
dart: A small pointed missile or a sudden movement
diva: A famous female opera or pop singer
dote: To be extremely and uncritically fond of
dual: Consisting of two parts, elements, or aspects
dune: A mound of sand formed by the wind
echo: A sound caused by the reflection of sound waves
envy: A feeling of discontented or resentful longing
epic: A long poem or story of heroic adventures
etch: To engrave a metal plate with acid
fawn: A young deer in its first year
feat: An achievement that requires great courage
fern: A flowerless plant with feathery fronds
flux: The action or process of flowing in or out
fray: A situation of intense activity or a worn edge
glut: An excessively abundant supply of something
gust: A brief, strong rush of wind
halo: A circle of light shown around a saint's head
hawk: A bird of prey with broad rounded wings
haze: A slight obscuration of the lower atmosphere
heir: A person legally entitled to property or rank
helm: A tiller or wheel for steering a ship
hull: The main body of a ship or a seed covering
icon: A person or thing regarded as a symbol
idyl: An extremely happy or peaceful scene
iris: A colored part of the eye or a flower

keen: Having or showing eagerness or enthusiasm
kiln: A furnace or oven for burning or drying pottery

leak: An accidental hole through which fluid escapes

lieu: Instead of; in the place of
loft: A room or space directly under the roof

lull: A temporary interval of quiet or lack of activity
lynx: A wild cat with yellowish-brown fur and tufted ears
lyric: Expressing the writer's emotions in stanzas

mica: A shiny silicate mineral with a layered structure

null: Having no legal or binding force; zero
oath: A solemn promise regarding one's future action
onyx: A gemstone with parallel colored layers
opus: A separate composition or set of compositions
oval: Having a rounded and slightly elongated outline
pact: A formal agreement between individuals or parties
peal: A loud ringing of a bell or bells
ploy: A cunning plan or action used to turn a situation
raft: A flat buoyant structure used as a boat
sash: A long strip of cloth worn over the shoulder
tint: A shade or variety of color
vibe: A person's emotional state or atmosphere
zeal: Great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause
